office_does: The county auditor runs elections, records property documents, issues vehicle and marriage licenses, and manages the county's accounting and financial reporting.
race_blurb: Two Republicans, both endorsed by the county GOP, compete for the short and full term after Auditor Michele Jaderlund retired in June. Appointed interim auditor Shannon Falstad, a 30-year county employee, led the primary 7,188 to 4,283 over Darci Homesley, who campaigns on fiscal responsibility and internal controls.

candidates.summary: Interim Grant County Auditor since July 2026 and 30-year county employee, including two decades in the auditor's recording, licensing, elections and accounting work.
highlights: Appointed interim auditor by the county commissioners effective July 1, 2026 [S4][S6]
In the auditor's office from 1996 to 2016, then accounting deputy in the clerk's office [S1][S6]
Priorities: election continuity, finishing the new accounting system, cross-training and retaining staff [S4][S7]

experience.basis: Appointed incumbent with about 20 years in the auditor's office and 30 in county government, running on continuity and institutional knowledge.

candidates.summary: Moses Lake business owner and county financial-services employee who runs on 35 years of accounting experience, fiscal responsibility and a non-partisan office.
highlights: Pledges rigorous internal controls to prevent waste and audits of county expenditures [S3]
Says county government should live within a budget like families do [S3]
Pledges a 'strictly non-partisan approach' to financial and election oversight [S3]

experience.basis: First-time candidate for elective office who runs on business and accounting experience from outside the auditor's office.

spending.basis: Platform centers on preventing waste and unnecessary spending, auditing county expenditures and living within a budget, repeated across her statement and website.
